Run the pptgo workflow: author or revise a slide deck, show it in the visual
editor, and export a native PPTX when asked.

## Tools

`deck_list` · `deck_new` · `slide_write` · `slide_read` · `deck_check` ·
`deck_open` · `deck_export`

## Steps

1. **Pick the project.** `deck_list` first. Create one with `deck_new` when the
   user is starting something new. Ask rather than guessing which existing deck
   they mean.
2. **Agree on the outline before drawing.** Page count and the one message per
   page, in a few lines. Skip this only for a small edit to an existing deck.
3. **Write each page** with `slide_write`, one complete SVG per call, page ids
   `P01`, `P02`, … in presentation order. Never paste slide SVG into the chat —
   it belongs in the tool call.
4. **Check** with `deck_check` and fix anything it reports as an error. Warnings
   are advisory; errors block the export.
5. **Show the result** with `deck_open`. Always end an authoring pass here, so
   the user sees the deck and can retype text directly in the editor.
6. **Export** with `deck_export` when the user wants the file. It runs
   finalize → quality gate → native PPTX and returns the .pptx path.

## SVG conventions (ppt-master)

- **Root**: `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1280" height="720"
  viewBox="0 0 1280 720" data-pptx-page-role="cover|toc|section|content|ending">`.
  `1280x720` is the canonical 16:9 canvas — not any other 16:9 size — and the
  `viewBox` is the coordinate authority.
- **Structure**: wrap each logical content unit in a top-level `<g id="…">`.
  Leave genuine page framing as root primitives carrying
  `data-pptx-role="background"` or `data-pptx-role="decoration"`.
- **Text**: `<text>` and `<tspan>` only. No `foreignObject`, no HTML. Manual line
  breaks are sibling `<tspan>` elements with their own `x` plus a `dy`.
- **Color**: uppercase `#RRGGBB`. Use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` instead
  of `rgba()`.
- **Fonts**: PowerPoint-safe families only — Microsoft YaHei, PingFang SC, Arial,
  Helvetica, Consolas.
- **Characters**: write typography as raw Unicode (— © → non-breaking space).
  Escape only `&` `<` `>` as `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;`. Never HTML named entities
  like `&nbsp;` or `&mdash;`.
- **Self-contained**: no external images, fonts, or stylesheets. Embed raster
  images as `data:` URIs.

Every element becomes a native, editable PowerPoint shape, so favour real shapes
and text over one big background image.

Reply in the user's language.
